SSHTron is a multiplayer lightcycle game that runs through SSH. Just run the command below and you'll be playing in seconds:
$ ssh sshtron.zachlatta.com
Controls: WASD or vim keybindings to move (
do not use your arrow keys
). Escape or Ctrl+C to exit.
Code quality disclaimer:
SSHTron was built in ~20 hours at
BrickHack 2
. Here be dragons.
Want to choose color yourself?
There are total 7 colors to choose from: Red, Green, Yellow, Blue, Magenta, Cyan and White
$ ssh red@sshtron.zachlatta.com
If the color you picked is already taken in all open games, you'll randomly be assigned a color.
Running Your Own Copy
Clone the project and
cd
into its directory. These instructions assume that you have your
GOPATH
setup correctly.
#
Create an RSA public/private keypair in the current directory for the server
#
to use. Don't give it a passphrase.
$ ssh-keygen -t rsa -f id_rsa
#
Download dependencies and compile the project
$ go get
&&
go build
#
Run it! You can set PORT to customize the HTTP port it serves on and SSH_PORT
#
to customize the SSH port it serves on.
$ ./sshtron
Running under a Docker container
Clone the project and
cd
into its directory.
#
Build the SSHTron Docker image
$ docker build -t sshtron
.
#
Spin up the container with always-restart policy
$ docker run -t -d -p 2022:2022 --restart always --name sshtron sshtron
For Raspberry Pi, use the following to build the Docker image:
$ docker build -t sshtron --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=resin/raspberry-pi-golang:latest
.
CVE-2016-0777
CVE-2016-0777
revealed two SSH client vulnerabilities that can be exploited by a malicious SSH server. While SSHTron does not exploit
these vulnerabilities, you should still patch your client before you play. SSHTron is open source, but the server
could always be running a modified version of SSHTron that does exploit the vulnerabilities described
in
CVE-2016-0777
.
If you haven't yet patched your SSH client, you can follow
these instructions
to do so now.

SSHTron is licensed under the MIT License. See the full license text in

44277245.article_summary: SSHTron是一款通过SSH运行的多人光线自行车游戏。玩家可以使用命令`$ ssh sshtron.zachlatta.com`快速加入游戏，并使用WASD或Vim键绑定进行控制。该项目在一次黑客马拉松中用约20小时开发完成，代码质量有所保留。玩家还可以通过指定颜色（如`$ ssh red@sshtron.zachlatta.com`）选择游戏角色，未指定时将随机分配。项目开源，并提供了在本地或Docker容器中运行自己副本的指南。此外，文章提醒玩家在游戏前修补SSH客户端以防止潜在的安全漏洞。SSHTron基于MIT许可证发布。
44277245.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款类似《Tron》电影中光线自行车游戏的怀旧与玩法讨论，涉及游戏体验、技术实现、以及对特定游戏功能或机制的建议和争议。

不同观点：
• Beloch认为，现有的光线自行车游戏无法像经典的80年代《Tron》电影中的那样忠实呈现那种紧张感和封闭感。虽然有像Armagetron这样的游戏，但其视角较远，缺乏未知和紧张的氛围。此外，Beloch指出新版《Tron》电影的游戏虽然不错，但并不是一回事，暗示可能存在未被充分服务的玩家群体。

• XiZhao将讨论重点转移到游戏的创造者Zach Latta以及其运营的非营利组织Hack Club，鼓励大家为该组织捐款，支持其培养高中技术人才的工作。

• Progbits表达了对Armagetron的怀旧情感，并提到当前游戏存在的问题：玩家可能因为其他玩家突然在自己面前生成而无故死亡，建议增加警告机制以改善体验。

• Wormius分享了自己的游戏高分体验，并以幽默的方式提到自己在不主动操作时反而表现更好，暗示游戏中可能存在运气成分或自动机制。

• Pathless对游戏的技术实现表示好奇，特别是其实时输入和播放功能，并将其与简单的文本传输进行比较，显示出对技术细节的关注。

• Dvh则对游戏中的速度机制提出建议，认为靠近赛道应增加速度，强调这是游戏中至关重要的元素，影响玩家的竞技体验。

• Joel以幽默的方式提出希望有人开发一款基于SSH的游戏（SSHnake），随后有人快速提供了相关链接，显示出社区的创造力和快速反应能力。

• Dijit简单分享了自己的高分体验，强调了游戏的趣味性。

补充讨论：
- 游戏机制的争议点在于玩家无故死亡的问题，progbits建议增加警告机制以提高公平性。
- 玩家对游戏速度机制的讨论（dvh的观点）显示出对竞技类游戏中平衡性的关注。
- 技术实现和游戏背后的非营利组织背景也被带入讨论，展示了更广泛的兴趣点。

data.title: Waymo's market share in San Francisco exceeds Lyft's
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: Waymo，谷歌母公司Alphabet旗下的自动驾驶公司，正在迅速崛起，预计在今年年底前可能成为旧金山最大的打车服务平台。根据YipitData的数据分析，Waymo的预约量在2024年大幅增长，从2023年8月的77,000次增至超过312,000次。其市场份额从零增长到超过25%，已经超过Lyft，并正快速逼近Uber。这一趋势导致依赖打车平台的独立承包司机收入锐减，面临失业风险。Waymo的成功不仅改变了旧金山的出行模式，也对当地经济和蓝领工人的生计构成威胁。虽然自动驾驶汽车提供了便捷服务，但也预示着潜在的经济和社会挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Waymo和Uber等打车服务的比较与争议

不同观点：
• **支持Waymo的体验**：[steelframe]和[moomoo11]对Waymo持积极态度，认为其乘坐体验顺畅、安全且价格合理，特别是在与糟糕的Uber体验对比后，更加倾向于Waymo。他们强调了Waymo在复杂交通情况下的处理能力以及整体舒适度。[moomoo11]甚至表示Waymo是近年来让他感到惊艳的少数科技产品之一。

• **对Waymo的保留意见**：[gonzalohm]对Waymo的服务有部分批评，指出其在转弯时出现问题，且等待时间过长。然而，相较于Uber司机的问题（如接单后取消或走错方向），[gonzalohm]还是认为Waymo更为可靠。

• **对未来发展的质疑**：[majormajor]对Waymo的长期可行性持观望态度，认为需要观察自动驾驶技术在未来几年内的发展及其基础设施的完善程度，尤其是价格点是否能吸引消费者成为车辆拥有者。

• **经济与社会影响**：[standardUser]讨论了Waymo等自动驾驶技术对蓝领工人生计的潜在影响，指出 rideshare模式本身已经备受批评，认为其带来的职业并非可持续。他暗示，消费者会选择更便宜、更安全的选项，而不论这些选项对工作岗位的影响。

• **对安全与法规的担忧**：[lvl155]担心机器人出租车可能引发的交通事故及其在法律上的处理难度，尤其是在当前 deregulation（放松监管）的环境下，这些问题可能变得更加复杂。

• **价格与市场竞争**：[emilsedgh]对Waymo未对Uber价格产生影响感到困惑，认为Waymo在解决一些体验问题后可能会对市场产生更大影响。[ChrisArchitect]提供了相关链接，指出即使Waymo价格更高，人们仍然愿意支付，显示出对Waymo服务的偏好。

补充讨论：
• **国际视角与文化差异**：[ENGNR]作为非美国居民，对无需支付小费表示欢迎，并认为这是吸引其访问美国的原因之一，显示出不同文化背景下对服务体验的不同期待。

• **市场竞争与用户流失**：[muglug]提到Lyft在旧金山因Waymo的竞争而受到更大影响，推测这可能与过去Uber因Travis Kalanick领导风格引发的负面形象有关。

• **服务可用性**：[jaredhallen]提到在尝试使用Waymo时发现其暂时无法运营，显示出服务可用性方面的挑战。

44277355.article_content:
If a data-backed trend plays out, Waymo could become San Francisco’s biggest ride-hailing service before the year ends.
Waymo’s celestial ascent into the cultural zeitgeist
— a rise that has been propelled by dystopian memes and sheer, futuristic novelty — has only been matched by how it continues swallowing its competition. The Alphabet-owned autonomous driving company saw explosive exponential growth in ridership in 2024, with driverless rides increasing from
77,000 to more than 312,000 lifts
by August of last year alone, according to the California DMV; as of publishing, Waymo asserts that 30% of their rides are to local small businesses.
Screenshot: Courtesy of YipitData
Independent contractors for Lyft and Uber have been
saying they’re “cooked”
for a while, citing massive declines in available requests as a result of Waymo’s success. (This, however, is a tandem issue: Waymo’s ride-hailing operations in San Francisco coincided with the increased number of regional rideshare drivers that began working during and after the pandemic.) But now factual data is showing that the aforementioned broiling is, indeed, happening … and at a rate quicker than once thought.
According to YipitData, a data and analytics firm based out of New York City, Waymo’s gross bookings from August of 2023 to April of this year have surpassed Lyft’s in market share. The twenty-month data analysis highlighted Uber’s dominance in San Francisco ridership — well over 50% of all trips booked via a ridesharing application were done on Uber throughout the analysis — but showed, perhaps more surprisingly, how quickly Waymo clambered into the commonplace. Waymo is also currently beating Lyft, a company that has operated rides in San Francisco since 2012, in total gross bookings.
In a staggeringly short amount of time, Waymo, which is about to celebrate its first anniversary of city-wide ride-hailing operations, has gone from effectively 0% market share of bookings in San Francisco to over 25%. Lyft has continuously gathered fewer bookings than Uber, but still managed to hold onto a roughly 30% market share since 2023.
Waymo has now flipped that stake, surpassing Lyft to become San Francisco’s second most-popular ride-hailing service. If the research published by YipitData is extrapolated outwardly, Waymo could easily beat Uber to become SF’s foremost taxi-like service by early next year. Or sooner.
What does this mean for San Francisco, the city that launched ridesharing services as we know them today? On the roads, not much; self-driving Jaguar iPaces would become even more prominent. But on an economic level, a subset of blue-collar workers (which numbers in the tens of thousands in San Francisco) would find themselves either regionally displaced or outright vocationally exterminated by a branch of artificial intelligence.
We don’t need a graph to tell you how that window into a
looming dystopian landscape plays out.
But hey, at least you won’t have to surrender to mind-numbing small talk on
your way to SFO.
Photo: Courtesy of Wikimedia Commons
Matt Charnock

data.title: Peeling the Covers Off Germany's Exascale "Jupiter" Supercomputer
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Jupiter是德国Forschungszentrum Jülich设施中首台达到百亿亿次级的超级计算机，采用混合CPU-GPU架构，由Eviden和ParTec建造。其主要计算性能来自GPU加速模块，在2025年6月的Top500排名中位列第四。尽管最初希望使用欧洲公司设计的自定义芯片，但Jupiter主要基于Nvidia的硬件。其通用集群模块采用SiPearl的Rhea1 Arm服务器CPU，拥有超过1300个节点，每个节点配备两个80核的Rhea1芯片，并配有64GB HBM内存。Rhea1原计划于2024年6月推出，预计今年晚些时候交付。Jupiter的GPU加速模块使用Nvidia的Grace G100 Arm服务器CPU和Hopper H200 GPU，每个节点包含两个计算模块，通过NVLink端口连接，提供高带宽数据传输。该系统标志着欧洲在高性能计算领域迈向芯片独立的一步，但仍依赖Nvidia技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲芯片自主与全球芯片产业的现状

不同观点：
• [supermatt] 认为欧洲在实现芯片自主上面临困难，但指出美国在芯片独立性方面也没有明显优势，直到最近，美国和欧洲都只能实现约12nm制程的芯片生产。他还提到，欧洲在芯片设计领域具有优势，尤其是在汽车和工业部门，且许多美国现代CPU在移动和嵌入式市场中使用基于Arm架构的设计，而Arm是欧洲（英国）的架构。

• [0x000xca0xfe] 关注GH200芯片上的CPU单元和GPU单元的尺寸对比，指出CPU单元不小于GPU单元，这一评论更侧重于技术细节和硬件架构上的观察。

• [theandrewbailey] 以幽默的方式提及"Jupiter"是否能运行"Jupyter"，虽然这是一个玩笑，但也反映了部分技术社区对命名相似性的有趣联想和轻松态度。

补充讨论：

• 技术细节的讨论如GH200芯片上CPU和GPU单元的尺寸对比，显示了技术社区对硬件架构的关注和兴趣。

• 幽默评论如"Jupiter"和"Jupyter"的命名联想，提供了一种轻松的讨论氛围，虽然不涉及实质技术问题，但体现了技术社区的互动风格。

44255770.article_content:
The newest of the exascale-class supercomputer to be profiled in the Top500 rankings in the June list is the long-awaited “Jupiter” system at Forschungszentrum Jülich facility in Germany. We finally have a sense of how this hybrid CPU-GPU machine will perform, although some of the details on its configuration are still not nailed down publicly.
Jupiter is the first exascale system to be completed under the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking of the European Union, and the fact that it is not using a custom CPU and XPU created by European companies, as was originally hoped, and is basically an Nvidia machine top to middle – bottom would include Nvidia storage, which it hasn’t acquired yet but will – speaks volumes about difficult it is to start from scratch to achieve chip independence for Europe. But, the Universal Cluster module will be based on the “Rhea1” Arm server CPU created by SiPearl, which is a step in the direction of independence for European HPC.
The Jupiter machine is built by Eviden, the HPC division of Atos that was going to be spun out but which the company has had second – and good – thoughts about doing, and ParTec, the German HPC system designer and installer.
Like its predecessor, the “Jewels” system that was first deployed in 2018 and upgraded a few times over the years, Jupiter is a hybrid supercomputer with blocks of CPU and GPU compute with other kinds of storage and acceleration blocks linked into it. With Jewels, the Cluster Module was installed first, based on Intel “Skylake” Xeon SP processors linked with 100 Gb/sec EDR InfiniBand from the then-independent Mellanox Technologies with everything installed in a BullSequana X1000 system from Eviden. In 2020, a BullSequana XH2000 system loaded up with AMD “Rome” Epyc CPUs and Nvidia “Ampere” GPU accelerators and called a Booster Module, was added to Jewels using 200 Gb/sec HDR InfiniBand.
Here is the honeycomb diagram for Jupiter, showing its modular components:
The vast majority of floating point and integer performance in Jupiter is, of course, in the GPU Booster module, which was taken for a spin using the High Performance LINPACK benchmark commonly used to rank supercomputer throughput and which
placed this Jupiter Booster module in the number four position on the June 2025 Top500 rankings
of supposedly HPC-centric systems.
The Universal Cluster will have more than CPU-only 1,300 nodes based on a pair of Rhea1 chips with 80 cores each based on the “Zeus” Neoverse V1 cores. These are the same V1 cores used in the “Graviton3” Arm chip designed by Amazon Web Services, which have a pair of 256-bit SVE vector engines. Each Rhea1 has a bank of 64 GB of HBM memory, the same fast but not fat memory used on GPU and XPU accelerators these days. As far as we know, the Rhea1 chip
was delayed back in June 2024
and is expected sometime later this year for FZJ. Some variant of SiPearl Arm CPU – maybe Rhea1 but also maybe its Rhea2 kicker – will also be employed in the second exascale system in Europe, called “Alice Recoque” and set to be hosted in France and presumably also to be built by Eviden. The Alice Recoque system has a budget of €542 million ($580.2 million), which includes money for the system, the facility, and its power and cooling.
This Universal Cluster is expected to have a mere 5 petaflops of FP64 performance running the HPL benchmark, which probably puts it at somewhere around 7 petaflops at peak theoretical performance. This is tiny compared to the Jupiter GPU Booster module that was tested for the June Top500 list.
The Jupiter GPU Booster node is based on a unique four-way clustering of Nvidia “Grace” G100 Arm server CPUs, which essentially uses four “Hopper” H200 GPUs as NUMA node controllers to link four CPUs and four GPUs into a more hefty cluster of eight compute engines working in harmony.
For those of you who didn’t see it
when we wrote about the Jupiter nodes back in September 2024
, here is a block diagram of the Jupiter GPU Booster node, which has a pair of sleds, each with a quad of Grace-Hopper modules linked by their main memories using direct NVLink ports off the CPUs and GPUs. Here is a block diagram of each node:
The H200 GPUs have 96 GB of HBM3 memory each, with 4 TB/sec of bandwidth across each accelerator. The single NVLink 4 ports that cross-link the four H200s together provide 300 GB/sec of bandwidth between them (150 GB/sec in each direction). Moreover, each Hopper GPU can communicate with the Grace CPU that hangs off of it at 600 GB/sec (300 GB/sec per direction) and to the other three CPUs in the quad complex at 100 GB/sec (50 GB/sec). Each CPU has a PCI-Express 5.0 port that reaches out to the 200 GB/sec ConnectX-6 SmartNIC. (With the “Blackwell” GPU designs, the GPUs link directly to the SmartNICs rather than having to go through the Grace CPUs.)
There are two compute sleds, each with a pair of Grace-Hopper superchips, in each Jupiter node, and there are also pair of dual-port 400 Gb/sec ConnectX-7 NDR InfiniBand

data.title: “Language and Image Minus Cognition”: An Interview with Leif Weatherby
data.author: Traces
data.article_summary: Leif Weatherby的著作《Language Machines》讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）引发的理论问题，尤其是“剩余人文主义”（remainder humanism）这一概念。剩余人文主义指的是一种将人类能力与机器对立的思维模式，无论是AI怀疑论者如Emily Bender和Noam Chomsky，还是AI风险研究者，都陷入了这种对立。Chomsky等人认为语言本质是认知，而机器只是模仿。与此同时，另一派则过度吹捧AI，设想超级智能的到来，同样忽视了实际技术。Weatherby主张，应从法国结构主义视角重新审视语言和文化系统，LLMs并非解决认知与文化分离的工具，但能促使我们重新审视这一问题。他批评当前人文领域对语言研究的忽视，呼吁重新参与这一讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类学习与大型语言模型（LLM）学习方式的比较，以及AI能力的局限性与未来发展

不同观点：
• [roenxi的观点] 认为人类和大型语言模型在处理和分类语言或图像时使用数据的方式不同。尽管人类日常通过感官（如视听）接收大量数据，但与ChatGPT等模型的训练数据量相比，人类在字符识别上花费的时间较少，且人类的学习过程涉及更多的物理和社会背景。虽然LLM和人类的学习方式明显不同，但人类使用的数据量并不少。

• [joe_the_user的观点] 认为任何对AI的“明确限制”的批评最终都会被超越，因为AI会逐渐超越这些设定的基准。提出“剩余理论”（remainder theory），认为我们不应试图定义AI不能做的事情，因为这些限制最终会被克服。同时，认为那些试图提出AI的“积极理论”（positive theory）的人实际上是在创造一种虚幻的实质感，因为这些理论所描述的能力可能会很快被AI实现。

补充讨论：
• [roenxi] 强调人类学习过程中的主动性和探索性（如追求新奇性），认为这是目前大型语言模型尚未具备的策略。
• [joe_the_user] 则侧重于AI能力的动态性和未来性，认为现在定义AI的局限性为时过早，因为这些局限性可能会随着技术进步而消失。

争议焦点：人类与AI在学习和处理信息上的本质区别以及AI未来是否能够完全超越这些区别。

by Robin Manley
Leif Weatherby
is an Associate Professor of German at New York University, where he directs the
Digital Theory Lab
. Robin Manley spoke with Dr. Weatherby about his latest book,
Language Machines: Cultural AI and the End of Remainder Humanism
(University of Minnesota Press, 2025), which argues that Large Language Models (LLMs) have effected a separation of cognition from language and computation in a form that corresponds to earlier structuralist theories.
Robin Manley:
In the introduction to
Language Machines
, you argue that today’s prevailing frameworks for AI research all share a common theoretical mistake, which you call “remainder humanism.” This goes for the AI-skeptical linguistic arguments made by scholars like
Emily Bender
and
Noam Chomsky
, but also for the more social-scientific literature on AI bias and ethics, and even for the otherwise quite-opposed tradition of AI risk and alignment research. What is remainder humanism, and how does it limit these different approaches to thinking about LLMs?
Leif Weatherby:
Remainder humanism is the term I use for us painting ourselves into a corner theoretically. The operation is just that we say, “machines can do x, but we can do it better or more
truly
.” This sets up a kind of John-Henry-versus-machine competition that guides the analysis. With ChatGPT’s release, that kind of lazy thinking, which had prevailed since the early days of AI critique, especially as motivated by the influential phenomenological work of
Hubert Dreyfus
, hit a dead end. If machines can produce smooth, fluent, and chatty language, it causes everyone with a stake in linguistic humanism to freak out. Bender retreats into the position that the essence of language is “speaker’s intent”; Chomsky claims that language is actually cognition, not words (he’s been doing this since 1957; his
NYT op-ed
from early 2023 uses examples from
Syntactic Structures
without adjustment).
But the other side are
also
remainder humanists. These are the boosters, the doomers, as well as the real hype people—and these amount to various brands of “rationalism,” as the internet movement around Eliezer Yudkowsky is unfortunately known. They basically
accept
the premise that machines are better than humans at everything, but then they ask, “What shall we do with our tiny patch of remaining earth, our little corner where we dominate?” They try to figure out how we can survive an event that is not occurring: the emergence of superintelligence. Their thinking aims to solve a very weak science fiction scenario justified by utterly incorrect mathematics. This is what causes them to devalue current human life, as has been
widely commented
.
Basically, we have two brands of “humanism” that both utterly fail to pay attention to the actual technologies at hand. The bright line between machine and human that they take as a premise prevents them from looking at language as such, and so allows them to go on letting either reference or intent be the essence of language. That’s a backhanded way of accepting the premise that cognition is utterly separate from culture, which is a serious scientific debate.
The position I take here is that LLMs don’t really solve that debate for human minds but do extend our ability to
see
truly cultural systems in action and give us some reasons to revisit that debate. Literary scholars dropped out of serious discussions of this type of issue about a generation ago, maybe even two, as I narrate polemically in chapter one, “How the Humanities Lost Language.” LLMs are calling us back into this world, to which we need to catch up fast.
RM:
In order to overcome these pitfalls, you turn to French structuralism—a tradition that articulated similar theoretical concerns long before LLMs. In the first chapter, you contrast the structuralist account of language with two others: the “syntactical” approach developed by Chomsky that was so pivotal in the development of linguistics and the “statistical” view that has been more influential in cognitive and data science. To be very schematic: in the syntactical view, the output of an LLM is nothing more than a party trick, as it has no relation to the internal cognitive laws of language; whereas in the statistical view, the output of an LLM is indistinguishable from human writing. How does LLM output appear in your structuralist view? What does this suggest for how we think about the familiar question of intelligence?
LW:
I’m not sure if the modelers would claim indistinguishability, though they seem bullish. It’s a weird area, which the book dwells on. On the one hand, we’re pretty sure these systems don’t do anything like what humans do to produce or classify language or images. They use massive amounts of data, whereas we seem to use relatively little; that data is highly structured, ours is not; etc. On the other hand, LLM outputs are indistinguishable from human writing in one important sense, which is that we have no tools to consistent

data.title: Seven replies to the viral Apple reasoning paper and why they fall short
data.author: spwestwood
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）是否具备真正的“思考”能力，以及其在处理复杂问题和推理任务中的表现和局限。

不同观点：
• thomasahle认为，人类在面对复杂问题和记忆需求时也存在困难，但我们可以合理地期望机器能做到人类不能做的事情。对于文章中提到的“人类也会犯这些错误，但我们仍然要求这些能力作为思考的定义”，thomasahle质疑这是否意味着人类的思考也是一种幻觉。
• neoden通过具体例子（汉诺塔问题）指出，人类在面对某些复杂问题时也需要借助外部工具，因此直接将人类与LLMs进行对比可能不公平。
• labrador指出，LLMs能够在遇到类似训练数据的问题时进行“推理”，但在面对全新问题时表现不佳。这种能力虽然不是真正的推理，但在许多情况下已经足够有用。
• ummonk认为，许多对LLMs的批评要么是无效的（例如人身攻击），要么被更重要的讨论点所涵盖。他强调，关键在于LLMs能否可靠地使用代码或逻辑系统，以及在没有工具辅助时产生错误答案是否表明其缺乏真正的推理能力。
• bluefirebrand对AI工具的炒作持批评态度，认为我们需要理性看待LLMs的能力，尽管它们在许多情况下是有用的，但过度炒作只会服务于那些在经济上投资于这些工具的人。
• brcmthrowaway指出，传统机器学习中不会在训练集中评估模型，而在LLMs中，所有数据都是训练集，这似乎是不正确的做法。
• hiddencost质疑Gary Marcus的专家地位，认为他多年来一直提出错误的观点，不应再被视为专家。
• avsteele提到，对于Apple论文的最佳批评并没有被这篇文章反驳。

补充讨论：
• skywhopper引用Salesforce论文中的重要观点，指出LLMs在保密意识方面表现接近于零。
• hrldcpr提供了原文链接，供有兴趣的读者查阅。
• thomasahle进一步讨论了LLMs能否通过编写代码来展示对问题的概念性理解，认为如果LLMs能编写出解决问题的代码，它们就显示出了概念性理解。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否具备真正的思考能力，尤其是面对全新问题时的推理能力。
• 对Gary Marcus的批评是否有效及其专家地位的质疑。
• 对LLMs过度炒作的担忧与其真实能力的理性评估之间的矛盾。

data.title: We investigated Amsterdam's attempt to build a 'fair' fraud detection model
data.author: troelsSteegin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了阿姆斯特丹市开发的一种机器学习模型，旨在识别需要进一步调查的福利申请。该模型使用了一种名为可解释提升机（EBM）的算法，通过分析申请者的行为和特征来预测“调查价值”，并生成风险评分。尽管模型没有直接使用性别或种族等敏感信息，但仍可能通过其他变量间接关联到特定群体。文章指出，尽管阿姆斯特丹在开发过程中努力确保模型的透明和公平，但其他地方如鹿特丹和法国社会保障机构在类似系统中忽视了对偏见的审查，导致对弱势群体的歧视。文章还提到，欧盟和纽约等地已开始通过立法限制高风险AI的使用，但构建公平的AI工具仍面临复杂挑战。最终，文章强调了在AI决策中实现公平的现实困难和持续努力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕阿姆斯特丹福利欺诈检测模型的公平性、有效性及其实施过程的讨论，包括模型中的偏差、公平定义的权衡以及模型性能问题。

不同观点：
• **tbrownaw** 和其他一些评论者认为，模型设计者意识到某些特征可能成为人口统计群体的代理变量，导致不公平的结果。这种不公平源于对不同群体关注度的权衡，即关注某一维度的公平（如减少基于种族/民族的差异）可能会损害其他维度的表现。这种权衡在模型中是不可避免的。
  
• **thatguymike** 和 **LorenPechtel** 对阿姆斯特丹项目的整体执行表示肯定。他们认为项目在伦理上建立了防护措施，并在无法满足公平标准时不部署模型，这是一种负责任的做法。然而，**LorenPechtel** 质疑过分关注“公平”是否必要，认为更应关注最小化错误率（假阳性和假阴性）。

• **GardenLetter27** 提出，虽然模型中未明确引用性别、种族等受保护的特征，但模型设计者应意识到这些特征可能通过其他相关变量成为代理变量。这并非种族主义，而是基于贝叶斯定理的正常现象。

• **bananaquant** 和 **BonoboIO** 批评模型的性能，认为模型的准确性不高（约67%的正预测准确率），其性能远低于高风险场景下应有的表现。他们质疑模型的实际效果，尤其是与系统有效性相关的指标（如真实阳性率、召回率）未被提及。

• **3abiton** 和 **octo888** 则关注模型复现性和数据处理问题。**3abiton** 指出，城市无法完全复现其分析结果，且模型偏差数据和已发布报告存在无法解释的差异，这让人质疑实验的可靠性。**octo888** 建议在标题中加入“福利”一词以更准确地描述情境。

• **ncruces** 和 **londons_explore** 提出更极端的观点。他们认为，在这些情况下实现完全公平是不可能的，主张采用完全随机的方式或通过补偿机制来减轻被错误调查者的负担。

补充讨论：
• **tomp** 和 **Jimmc414** 强调，不同公平标准之间的冲突是数学上的现实问题，难以同时满足所有标准。训练模型时，过去的人类决策偏差不可避免地被引入模型中，从而影响模型的公平性。

• **zeroCalories** 关注“重新加权”的实际操作，询问这是否意味着对某些群体的错误分类进行更多惩罚，或确保各群体在数据中均匀分布。

争议焦点：
• 模型中的公平性定义和权衡：是否应优先考虑某些群体的利益，即使这可能损害其他群体的表现。
• 模型的实际效果和有效性：在准确性不足的情况下，模型的部署价值和意义受到质疑。
• 数据处理和复现性问题：实验的可靠性和结果的可信度受到质疑。

总结：讨论围绕模型的公平性、准确性和数据处理的可靠性展开，各方对如何实现公平、模型性能的标准以及实际操作中的问题提出了不同见解。

For the past four years, Lighthouse has investigated welfare fraud detection algorithms deployed in five European countries. Our investigations have found evidence that these systems discriminated against vulnerable groups with oftentimes steep consequences for people’s lives.
Governments and companies deploying these systems often show little regard for the biases they perpetrate against vulnerable groups. The city of Rotterdam told us that it had never run code designed to test whether its model was disproportionately flagging vulnerable groups. France’s social security agency, CNAF, confirmed to us that it had never audited its model for bias.
In January of 2023, three months before publishing our investigation into Rotterdam’s risk scoring algorithm, we sent a public records request to the city of Amsterdam, one of Europe’s most progressive capitals. Among other things, we asked for documents, code and data relating to a similar system Amsterdam had been developing. Given that we had fought over a year to obtain these types of material in other investigations, we were surprised when the city immediately complied with our request.
The materials disclosed by the city were related to a machine learning model it was developing in order to predict which of the city’s residents were most likely to have submitted an incorrect application for welfare. At the time of our public records request, the model was still in development. The overall development goal for the model, according to the city’s internal documentation, was to have fewer welfare applicants investigated, but a higher share of those investigated rejected. Internal documents also emphasized two other aims: avoid bias against vulnerable groups, and outperform human caseworkers.
After reading through the documentation, it quickly became clear to us why the city had been so forthcoming. The city had gone to significant lengths in order to develop a model that was transparent and treated vulnerable groups fairly.
We wanted to investigate whether the city of Amsterdam had succeeded in developing a fair model. Over the course of eight months, we ran a series of our own tests on the model and data containing real world outcomes for people flagged as suspicious by the model. When it came to the outcome data, the city ran our own tests locally and returned aggregate results in order to comply with European data protection laws.
The past five years have seen a number of regulatory efforts to reign in harmful uses of AI. The EU AI Act, passed in 2024, will require AI systems deemed “high risk” to be registered with the European Commission. In New York City, employers have been prohibited from screening employees using AI without conducting bias audits since July 2023. Meanwhile, the private sector, academics and multilateral institutions have produced a number of responsible AI frameworks. In taking on this investigation, we wanted to look ahead and understand the thorny reality of building a fair AI tool that makes consequential decisions about people’s lives.
The code and data underlying our analysis can be found on our
Github
.
How the model works
The City of Amsterdam’s model aimed to identify applications for further investigation. Staff members check for applications that contain mistakes and redirect any concerning applications to an investigator. The model is designed to replicate this first screening.
A flagged application is not automatically rejected. However, investigators are empowered to request a beneficiary’s bank statements, summon them for meetings, and even visit their homes. Past reporting, including our own, has shown how these investigations can be a stressful or even traumatising experience.
The model uses a type of algorithm called an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). EBMs prioritize explainability — the degree to which an AI algorithm is understandable instead of being a confusing “black box” of abstract mathematical processes. Amsterdam’s EBM model predicts ‘investigation worthiness’ based on variables that measure welfare applicants’ behavior and characteristics, features.
Model predictions are based on 15 features. None of these features explicitly referred to an applicant’s gender or racial background, as well as other demographic characteristics protected by anti-discrimination law. But the model designers were aware that features could be correlated with demographic groups in a way that would make them proxies.

44257862.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了阿姆斯特丹市开发的一种机器学习模型，旨在识别需要进一步调查的福利申请。该模型使用了一种名为可解释提升机（EBM）的算法，通过分析申请者的行为和特征来预测“调查价值”，并生成风险评分。尽管模型没有直接使用性别或种族等敏感信息，但仍可能通过其他变量间接关联到特定群体。文章指出，尽管阿姆斯特丹在开发过程中努力确保模型的透明和公平，但其他地方如鹿特丹和法国社会保障机构在类似系统中忽视了对偏见的审查，导致对弱势群体的歧视。文章还提到，欧盟和纽约等地已开始通过立法限制高风险AI的使用，但构建公平的AI工具仍面临复杂挑战。最终，文章强调了在AI决策中实现公平的现实困难和持续努力。
44257862.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕阿姆斯特丹福利欺诈检测模型的公平性、有效性及其实施过程的讨论，包括模型中的偏差、公平定义的权衡以及模型性能问题。

不同观点：
• **tbrownaw** 和其他一些评论者认为，模型设计者意识到某些特征可能成为人口统计群体的代理变量，导致不公平的结果。这种不公平源于对不同群体关注度的权衡，即关注某一维度的公平（如减少基于种族/民族的差异）可能会损害其他维度的表现。这种权衡在模型中是不可避免的。
  
• **thatguymike** 和 **LorenPechtel** 对阿姆斯特丹项目的整体执行表示肯定。他们认为项目在伦理上建立了防护措施，并在无法满足公平标准时不部署模型，这是一种负责任的做法。然而，**LorenPechtel** 质疑过分关注“公平”是否必要，认为更应关注最小化错误率（假阳性和假阴性）。

• **GardenLetter27** 提出，虽然模型中未明确引用性别、种族等受保护的特征，但模型设计者应意识到这些特征可能通过其他相关变量成为代理变量。这并非种族主义，而是基于贝叶斯定理的正常现象。

• **bananaquant** 和 **BonoboIO** 批评模型的性能，认为模型的准确性不高（约67%的正预测准确率），其性能远低于高风险场景下应有的表现。他们质疑模型的实际效果，尤其是与系统有效性相关的指标（如真实阳性率、召回率）未被提及。

• **3abiton** 和 **octo888** 则关注模型复现性和数据处理问题。**3abiton** 指出，城市无法完全复现其分析结果，且模型偏差数据和已发布报告存在无法解释的差异，这让人质疑实验的可靠性。**octo888** 建议在标题中加入“福利”一词以更准确地描述情境。

• **ncruces** 和 **londons_explore** 提出更极端的观点。他们认为，在这些情况下实现完全公平是不可能的，主张采用完全随机的方式或通过补偿机制来减轻被错误调查者的负担。

补充讨论：
• **tomp** 和 **Jimmc414** 强调，不同公平标准之间的冲突是数学上的现实问题，难以同时满足所有标准。训练模型时，过去的人类决策偏差不可避免地被引入模型中，从而影响模型的公平性。

• **zeroCalories** 关注“重新加权”的实际操作，询问这是否意味着对某些群体的错误分类进行更多惩罚，或确保各群体在数据中均匀分布。

争议焦点：
• 模型中的公平性定义和权衡：是否应优先考虑某些群体的利益，即使这可能损害其他群体的表现。
• 模型的实际效果和有效性：在准确性不足的情况下，模型的部署价值和意义受到质疑。
• 数据处理和复现性问题：实验的可靠性和结果的可信度受到质疑。

总结：讨论围绕模型的公平性、准确性和数据处理的可靠性展开，各方对如何实现公平、模型性能的标准以及实际操作中的问题提出了不同见解。

主要讨论点：Commodore 64及其冻结卡带的技术原理、实现方式以及相关硬件的讨论，同时涉及与其他平台（如Atari 8-bit和Amiga）的比较。

不同观点：
• michalpleban认为，运行在Commodore 64上的软件可以通过自行触发NMI中断，并保持NMI线路低电平，从而防止被冻结技术中断。他具体解释了通过使用第二个CIA芯片来实现这一点的机制。
• erwincoumans回顾了过去使用Power Cartridge的经历，并提到自己曾通过逆向工程实现了类似功能，如保存/恢复游戏、加速加载和截图功能，展示了当时对硬件卡带的深入研究和改造。
• sfjailbird回忆了自制冻结卡带的历史，指出当时这类卡带的制造和流通情况，强调了这些卡带的实用性和受欢迎程度，尽管当时对背后的技术细节不甚了解。
• classichasclass对比了不同类型的冻结卡带，表达了对FC3接口的喜爱，但指出在NTSC系统上使用时遇到的问题，因此更常使用其他替代卡带如ICEPIC或Super Snapshot。
• daitangio对Commodore 64代码的复杂性和精简性表示惊叹，强调了在极少字节数下实现复杂功能的编程技巧。
• predictsoft将Commodore 64的冻结功能与Amiga 1200上的Action Replay软盘功能作对比，指出Amiga可以通过软件直接利用高地址空间加载，而无需额外硬件支持，暗示软件解决方案有时更为灵活。
• TMWNN讨论了Atari 8-bit系统上没有冻结卡带的原因，推测是由于缺乏Ultimax-style bypass机制，同时提到Atari 8-bit的设计使得FujiNet可以无需像Commodore系统那样的变通方法或缺点，暗示了不同硬件架构对类似功能实现的影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同平台（Commodore 64、Atari 8-bit、Amiga）之间的技术差异和实现类似功能的不同方法，特别是硬件和软件解决方案的对比。
• 冻结卡带的技术不仅涉及到防止程序被中断，还涉及到快速加载、保存游戏等实用功能，展示了当时用户对C64等平台的深度定制能力。
• 争议的焦点在于冻结技术的实现方法和可行性，特别是软件是否能够主动防止被冻结，这引发了对NMI中断机制的深入讨论。

data.title: Debunking HDR [video]
data.author: plastic3169
data.article_summary: 这篇文章旨在揭露和澄清有关HDR（高动态范围）和SDR（标准动态范围）之间的一些误解和技术细节。文章首先介绍了基础概念，包括人类对色调的相对感知以及颜色空间的理解。随后，文章比较了SDR和HDR的颜色空间，讨论了两者转换的解决方案。文章还分析了市场上对HDR的一些误导性宣传，如效率问题、色域误解以及创作者意图与自动化处理的冲突。最后，文章提出了应对建议，并总结了要点，强调色调的艺术性而非纯粹的技术性处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于视频色彩理论和HDR与SDR技术的分析和讨论

不同观点：
• **[_wire_]**: 认为视频对色彩理论的应用进行了扎实的概述，但指出视频在开篇未能明确提出要辩驳的论点。视频的核心是比较SDR和HDR，指出HDR提供了更高的保真度，但最终视觉效果的价值仍取决于创作者的创意。同时，强调了人类视觉适应的动态范围差异，并通过对比100:1和数十亿:1的感知窗口解释了HDR的优势。

• **[dcrazy]**: 对视频中颜色空间和术语的简化表示不满，指出Yedlin在RGB三元组和颜色空间坐标之间的混淆，并强调Rec. 2100不仅定义了颜色空间，还定义了传输函数（PQ和HLG），这些细节在视频中被忽略了。不过，对视频中的一些类比（如英尺/米转换）表示赞赏。

• **[nayuki]**: 更关注视频的技术传输质量，称赞视频的无缓冲加载速度和用户界面响应速度，对比YouTube的缓慢体验，认为多亿级公司提供的用户体验不如一个简单的视频文件。

• **[IshKebab]**: 认为视频过长且没有在开头明确指出要辩驳的内容，希望得到简明的总结。

• **[sansseriff]**: 对Yedlin的视频表示赞赏，但希望他能分享代码以促进开源色彩分级软件的开发，指出由于色彩分级工具多为专有，科学研究的开放性受限。

• **[virtualritz]**: 提到在Android设备上观看视频时遇到的全屏退出问题，认为这是一个奇怪的Chrome/Android bug。

• **[magicalhippo]**: 快速浏览视频后，感觉视频内容类似于讨论24位音频是否必要，并分享了自己从SDR到HDR的早期技术体验，希望看到更高动态范围的显示效果。

• **[ttoinou]**: 认为Yedlin指出的SDR输入在某些情况下与HDR相似是显而易见的，但强调HDR不仅是一个数学转换公式，更是一种新的交流方式。同时，对Yedlin的“所有图像都适用”的观点表示怀疑，认为HDR为创意提供了更广阔的色彩空间。

• **[autobodie]**: 对视频内容表示强烈赞同，提到阅读过相关书籍，认为HDR和SDR的问题与ACES有很大重叠，并将广泛分享此视频。

• **[FrostKiwi]**: 对视频使用Nuke完成表示赞赏，认为其体现了技术和艺术的完美结合。

• **[naikrovek]**: 将30位色彩与16位色彩的过渡进行对比，认为HDR的销售宣传夸大了实际视觉差异，指出显示器制造商通过HDR模式锁定某些功能以促进销售。

• **[empiricus]**: 认为应从接近现实的捕捉开始，然后进行创意处理，SDR类似于黑白电影，而HDR有潜力实现更真实的视觉效果，但目前电影制作者尚未充分利用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于HDR与SDR的实际视觉差异以及HDR技术的必要性。部分观众认为HDR提供了更大的创作空间和更高的保真度，而另一些观众则认为这种差异被夸大，且HDR技术可能被商家利用以促进销售。

• 视频的技术细节和术语使用也引发了讨论，部分观众认为Yedlin在解释颜色空间和传输函数时过于简化，导致信息传递不够准确。

• 视频的技术传输质量和用户体验得到了部分观众的好评，尤其是与YouTube的对比。

• 开源色彩分级软件的提议得到了关注，但受限于当前专有工具的广泛使用，这一提议实现起来可能面临挑战。

• **[autobodie]**: 对视频内容表示强烈赞同，提到阅读过相关书籍，认为HDR和SDR的问题与ACES有很大重叠，并将广泛分享此视频。

• **[FrostKiwi]**: 对视频使用Nuke完成表示赞赏，认为其体现了技术和艺术的完美结合。

• **[naikrovek]**: 将30位色彩与16位色彩的过渡进行对比，认为HDR的销售宣传夸大了实际视觉差异，指出显示器制造商通过HDR模式锁定某些功能以促进销售。

• **[empiricus]**: 认为应从接近现实的捕捉开始，然后进行创意处理，SDR类似于黑白电影，而HDR有潜力实现更真实的视觉效果，但目前电影制作者尚未充分利用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于HDR与SDR的实际视觉差异以及HDR技术的必要性。部分观众认为HDR提供了更大的创作空间和更高的保真度，而另一些观众则认为这种差异被夸大，且HDR技术可能被商家利用以促进销售。

• 视频的技术细节和术语使用也引发了讨论，部分观众认为Yedlin在解释颜色空间和传输函数时过于简化，导致信息传递不够准确。

• 视频的技术传输质量和用户体验得到了部分观众的好评，尤其是与YouTube的对比。

• 开源色彩分级软件的提议得到了关注，但受限于当前专有工具的广泛使用，这一提议实现起来可能面临挑战。

data.title: Python argparse has a limitation on argument groups that makes me sad
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何某些浏览器访问博客或wiki时会被阻止。原因在于，为了应对2025年初大量使用旧浏览器用户代理的高流量爬虫（包括用于LLM训练的数据采集），网站采取了封锁措施。如果用户使用最新浏览器却仍被误拦，可联系作者。特别提到，archive.*（如archive.today等）的爬虫因使用旧Chrome用户代理并模仿恶意IP，也被屏蔽，建议使用行为更规范的archive.org进行存档。作者是Chris Siebenmann，2025-02-17发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python程序中处理命令行参数的默认值与用户提供值的优先级问题，以及如何设计参数结构以支持灵活的配置管理。

不同观点：
• [mjevans] 提出是否存在标准Python库来标注一个参数是用户提供的还是默认值，这对于配置优先级管理非常重要。程序的默认值应具有最低优先级，依次被配置文件、命令行参数和运行时更改的配置所覆盖。

• [xg15] 认为设计上可以通过使用如`--foo-timeout=0`来表示禁用某个特定超时，而不是使用`--no-timeouts`来禁用所有超时。这种设计允许用户灵活地控制每个超时，而不是全部一起控制。同时，提出是否可以通过定义别名来实现`--no-timeouts`。

• [NewsaHackO] 建议通过编写一个函数来生成所有参数组，并将每个参数（如`--notimeout`, `--timeout-x`）传递给解析器，以此简化参数的管理。

• [qwertox] 指出问题不在于`add_mutually_exclusive_group`，而在于`argparse`缺少内部机制来优雅地处理这种参数需求。如果不互斥的参数就不应该放在互斥组中。

• [looknee] 提供了一个实际案例，说明gcloud CLI如何使用`argparse`来处理这种情况，通过父互斥组包含一个`--no-timeout`标志和另一个包含具体超时标志的子组。

补充讨论：
• [lordkrandel] 简单表示对该问题的认同，认为确实是个麻烦的问题。

争议焦点：
• 如何设计命令行参数以支持灵活的配置和默认值覆盖逻辑，特别是如何处理多个超时参数的禁用功能。不同的设计方案包括使用`--no-timeouts`完全禁用所有超时与通过特定参数如`--foo-timeout=0`分别控制每个超时。

• `argparse`库的功能限制，尤其是如何在不使用互斥组的情况下处理复杂的参数关系。

44249344.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: GitHub's CEO says startups can only get so far with vibe coding
data.author: kmdupree
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用“vibe coding”（依赖AI辅助编程）在开发中的作用和效果的讨论，以及AI在创业公司和技术投资中的影响。

不同观点：
• **fnordpiglet**：认为vibe coding在项目的初始阶段非常有用，可以帮助处理许多基础性、琐碎的设计决策。但当项目复杂度增加时，AI往往会陷入局部最小值，难以继续推进，最终需要更有经验的工程师接手。他将这种体验比作与有4年经验的工程师合作，能够解决一定问题，但面对复杂问题时仍需更有经验的人来领导。

• **nico**：提出创业公司在初期通过AI辅助编程来快速构建系统并推向市场，可以更早获得投资者的青睐。即使后期需要更多人力投入，早期通过AI节省成本和时间可能会吸引更多投资，形成一种“超精益公司”模式。

• **duxup**：对“vibe coding”这一概念表示困惑，认为它似乎是为了吸引媒体关注而创造的词汇，而非一个明确的技术概念。

• **sherdil2022**：支持nico的观点，认为nico的评论具有一定的合理性。

• **jamesgill**：质疑AI在实际商业环境中的应用，提到微软（GitHub的拥有者）在AI上投入巨大资金（800亿美元），暗示AI技术尚未成熟到能完全替代人类开发者，公司仍然需要大量投资来推进AI相关技术。

补充讨论：
• **fnordpiglet**的评论中提到了AI在处理工具库和细节方面的能力，但也指出了AI在面对复杂问题时的局限性，强调了人类工程师经验的重要性。
• **nico**则侧重于AI在商业和创业环境中的潜力，认为AI可以帮助创业公司快速成长，即使在后期需要更多人力投入，早期的优势仍然明显。
• **duxup**和**sherdil2022**的评论则反映了部分人对“vibe coding”这一新兴概念的理解和态度，有人表示困惑，有人表示支持。
• **jamesgill**的评论引入了大公司（如微软）在AI领域的巨额投资，质疑AI在当前技术水平下能否真正替代人类开发者，并指出AI技术本身仍需大量资源支持。

争议焦点：AI在编程中的实际效用和局限性，以及在创业公司和技术投资中的潜在影响。

data.title: Show HN: Qrkey – Offline private key backup on paper
data.author: techwolf12
data.article_summary: **QRKey** 是一个命令行工具，用于生成和恢复用于离线私钥备份的QR码。它可以将文件转换为QR码并打印或存储，随后通过扫描这些QR码恢复文件。该工具支持大文件，可将文件拆分为多个QR码，并包含元数据以便于恢复和验证。用户可以通过Homebrew或Docker安装和使用该工具。主要功能包括从文件生成包含QR码的PDF，以及从PDF或文本文件中扫描QR码恢复文件。项目采用MIT许可证，已获得136个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过打印存储和恢复私钥等敏感信息的安全性与技术实现

不同观点：
• **krunck** 提醒要注意打印设备的安全性，很多办公环境的打印机/复印机可以存储打印数据，技术人员可能访问这些数据，存在泄露风险。
• **cornstalks** 提出结合Shamir’s secret sharing方案，将私钥分给家庭成员，以备不时之需。同时也提到家庭成员不懂技术，实现起来有难度。
• **slig** 对打印私钥的安全性提出质疑，考虑到打印机软件、固件漏洞及网络连接的潜在风险。
• **saclark11** 推荐了PaperAge工具，该工具可以将私钥加密后生成纸质备份，但需要确保不忘记密码短语或做好备份。
• **kardianos** 分享了自己为keepass数据库开发的工具，用于生成可打印的密钥表，并存储在保险箱中，强调了结合密码管理工具的使用。
• **qualeed** 质疑使用QR码的必要性，认为直接打印可读文档也可以实现存储，并询问QR码的特定使用场景。
• **hypeatei** 对项目使用Docker镜像表示不解，认为简单的命令行工具不需要Docker，直接通过git clone即可，特别是Go语言开发的应用。
• **RamRodification** 指出文档中的一个命令行示例可能有误，生成的QR码是PDF格式，但恢复时却要求输入txt文件，可能存在不一致。
• **_whiteCaps_** 分享了自己的类似方案，使用GPG备份，并提到使用高质量的打印纸提高打印质量。
• **thayne** 认为这个想法不错，但由于没有打印机且不愿意将私钥交由公共电脑和打印机处理，所以对他不实用。
• **tantalor** 纠正了一个错误，指出条形码扫描仪不能扫描QR码，因此通过QR码恢复数据需要专门的QR码扫描器。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到打印设备和工具的安全性问题，特别是非个人设备可能带来的泄露风险。
• 关于是否使用QR码，部分人认为直接打印文本也可以，但其他人指出QR码在自动化处理和便捷性上的优势。
• 涉及到一些技术实现细节，如Shamir’s secret sharing和特定工具（如PaperAge、keepass插件）的推荐和使用经验。
• 争议焦点在于打印私钥的安全性与便捷性之间的权衡，以及使用QR码的实际意义和操作准确性。

QRKey
qrkey
is a command-line tool for generating and recovering QR codes from files for offline private key backup.
It allows you to convert files into QR codes that can be printed or stored, and later recovered from those QR codes.
It supports large files by splitting them into multiple QR codes, and includes metadata for easy recovery and validation.
Convert a file into a PDF with QR codes
Recover from a PDF with QR codes with a barcode scanner
Recover from a PDF with QR codes from a file with lines
Installation
macOS users can install
qrkey
using Homebrew Tap:
brew tap techwolf12/tap
brew install techwolf12/tap/qrkey
For Docker users, you can use the Docker image:
docker run -v
"
$(
pwd
)
"
:/mnt ghcr.io/techwolf12/qrkey:latest generate --in /mnt/testfile.txt --out /mnt/test.pdf
For other systems, see the
releases page
.
Usage
To generate a QR code from a file, use the following command:
qrkey generate --in
<
file
>
--out file.pdf
To recover a file from QR codes, use the following command:
qrkey recover --in
<
file.txt
>
Or to recover interactively:
qrkey recover

44268545.article_summary: **QRKey** 是一个命令行工具，用于生成和恢复用于离线私钥备份的QR码。它可以将文件转换为QR码并打印或存储，随后通过扫描这些QR码恢复文件。该工具支持大文件，可将文件拆分为多个QR码，并包含元数据以便于恢复和验证。用户可以通过Homebrew或Docker安装和使用该工具。主要功能包括从文件生成包含QR码的PDF，以及从PDF或文本文件中扫描QR码恢复文件。项目采用MIT许可证，已获得136个星标。

data.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting: Our Search for a Time-Series Foundation Model
data.author: tiwarinitish86
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了时间序列预测领域中“基础模型”（foundation models）的兴起，这些模型旨在通过大规模预训练来适应多种数据流和领域，而无需为每个场景单独训练模型。作者对比了传统模型如ARIMA和Prophet，指出其在面对多样化数据时的局限性，并介绍了亚马逊、谷歌、IBM和Datadog的最新时间序列基础模型（Amazon Chronos、Google TimesFM、IBM Tiny Time-Mixers、Datadog Toto）。

文章详细描述了这些新模型的评估方法，包括使用多变量预测任务和真实数据源。通过实验，作者评估了这些模型在零样本预测（zero-shot forecasting）中的表现，发现基础模型在处理不同类型的时间序列数据时展现了较强的泛化能力，能够有效减少手动调参和重新训练的工作量。

最终，作者认为时间序列基础模型具有巨大的潜力，特别是在可观察性数据处理方面，能够显著提升预测效率和适应性。未来，进一步优化和应用这些模型将是关键。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：时间序列基础模型（foundation model）的有效性、应用及其评估方法

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby认为，博客中对时间序列基础模型的定义有误。基础模型应该具备处理训练目标任务之外的多任务能力，而博客中讨论的是无需重新训练的分布外预测。Fripplebubby指出，现有的ARIMA和Prophet模型已经很好地解决了这个问题，且重新拟合模型只需很短的时间。此外，他认为LLM架构是否能提升单变量或多变量时间序列预测任务仍未有明确答案。

• wenc提到了Makridakis竞赛的历史结论，即复杂的统计方法未必比简单方法提供更准确的预测。wenc质疑当前是否情况有变，并引用了Nixtla与Chronos团队在相关问题上的争论。

• spmurrayzzz表示对Autogluon自动拟合/评估方法的结果感兴趣，并猜测加权平均模型可能会表现更好。

• nikhil4usinha关注模型的实际应用场景，尤其是异常检测方面的用例。

• fumeux_fume对结果表中模型是否在相同数据集上测试表示困惑，并建议提供测试数据和预测的可视化图表以增加透明度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是时间序列基础模型的定义及其评估标准是否恰当。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同评估方法和数据集的选择对模型表现的影响。
• 测试方法的科学性和评估指标的合理性也是讨论中的重要议题。

这些观点共同构成了对时间序列基础模型及其应用的多元看法，涉及模型评估、测试方法、应用场景等多个方面。

Parseable is a new and rapidly growing project focused on delivering fast and seamless observability on S3. If you love what we're building, show us some ❤️ by

Now, let's dive into the blog!
Introduction
In the last few years, the field of time-series forecasting has seen a fundamental shift. Where we once depended solely on classic statistical methods, think
ARIMA
,
SARIMA
, and
Prophet
, new “foundation” models have emerged, promising to bring the power and flexibility of large language models (LLMs) into the world of time-series data. The allure is obvious: can we build a single, reusable forecasting model that works across a variety of datasets and domains, instead of painstakingly training a new model for every scenario?
Parseable
is built to handle our users’ observability data at any scale, a nonstop stream of raw ingest counts, infrastructure vitals, and fine-grained application signals. Running a separate, hand-tuned forecasting model for every slice quickly turns into a treadmill: each new stream or workload tweak demands fresh hyper-params, retrains, and ever-growing config sprawl. All that manual churn slows forecasts and breeds drift, so the results never feel fully trustworthy.
Then came the rise of foundation models, which revolutionised natural language processing by offering strong zero-shot and transfer learning capabilities. Researchers began asking a natural question: if LLMs can generalise to new tasks with minimal retraining, could similar techniques be applied to time-series data? What if you could just hand any telemetry stream to a pre-trained foundation model and immediately get a high-quality forecast, regardless of whether the model had seen data from that source before?
Motivated by this possibility, we set out to benchmark a new generation of time-series foundation models,
Amazon Chronos
,
Google TimesFM
,
IBM Tiny Time-Mixers
, and
Datadog Toto
.
Our goal was to assess how well these models perform on two representative tasks: a relatively straightforward forecasting problem (predicting ingestion volumes) and a more complex multivariate problem (forecasting multiple pod-level metrics). Along the way, we compared them to classical baselines and took note of both practical and technical trade-offs.
This post details our methodology, the challenges we encountered, how we evaluated the models, and what we learned from putting foundation models to the test on real-world observability data.
Why Foundation Models?
The idea of “foundation models” has fundamentally changed how we approach complex machine learning problems. In natural language processing, models like GPT have shown that a single, large model trained on vast and diverse datasets can generalize well to entirely new tasks sometimes even without fine-tuning. This zero-shot capability means a single model can perform sentiment analysis, summarization, translation, or question-answering, just by changing the prompt.
In the world of time-series forecasting, the appeal of such flexibility is obvious, especially for modern data engineering and observability platforms. Traditionally, every new data stream whether it’s CPU utilization, request rates, or disk I/O required its own model, hyperparameter tuning, and regular retraining. For an SRE or platform engineer, this quickly becomes unmanageable as the number of streams explodes. If a pipeline ingests data from a hundred microservices, does every service metric really need its own hand-tuned ARIMA or Prophet model? The answer, up until recently, was “yes.”
Foundation models for time series are built to change that. The core motivation is scalability and adaptability: train a single, large model (often with billions of parameters) on a wide range of time-series datasets and let it learn the underlying “language” of temporal data. Once trained, this model should ideally handle a completely new telemetry stream, even if it has never seen data of that exact shape or domain before. In theory, you could input any new time series, whether it’s network packet counts, database query durations, or energy consumption readings and get a high-quality forecast without retraining.

data.title: A dark adtech empire fed by fake CAPTCHAs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 2024年，安全研究人员发现克里姆林宫支持的虚假信息活动利用恶意广告技术绕过社交媒体审核，传播亲俄罗斯的虚假新闻。这些活动通过一个名为“Doppelganger”的网络进行，该网络使用复杂的“域名伪装”技术，使虚假信息网站在线时间更长，并确保只有特定受众能看到内容。Doppelganger与VexTrio共享基础设施，后者是一个恶意流量分发系统，管理来自钓鱼网站和社交工程诈骗的流量。研究显示，Doppelganger的伪装服务还推广成人约会网站，如LosPollos和TacoLoco，这些网站通过入侵WordPress网站获取流量，并利用诱导性通知进行诈骗。Adspro Group运营这些服务，其基础设施由瑞士 hosting providers C41和Teknology SA提供支持，最终追溯到由Giulio Vitorrio Leonardo Cerutti拥有的公司。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TacoLoco网络使用欺骗性手段通过浏览器推送通知进行流量变现，以及相关技术和社会工程学诈骗的问题。

不同观点：
• LegionMammal978：分享了亲身经历，一位老年亲属曾被TacoLoco的推送通知骚扰，表明这种欺骗性手段对不熟悉技术的用户影响很大。他通过设置浏览器自动拒绝通知来解决问题。
• preinheimer：认为通过“点击按钮证明你是人类”的诈骗手段很巧妙，能有效欺骗用户。
• justusthane：对为何在访问虚假新闻内容前要经过多个域名跳转表示不解，并询问这种行为的目的。
• b0a04gl：将这种推送通知视为新的弹出广告，认为浏览器赋予其过多的前台展示权限，且未征求用户同意。
• psychoslave：指出TacoLoco的流量分配系统（TDS）主要管理来自钓鱼、恶意软件和社会工程诈骗的受害者流量，并批评合法广告网络的类似操作。
• thyristan：批评浏览器在权限请求和管理方面的用户界面设计混乱，建议统一权限请求和更改流程，增加更多的控制选项。
• tempodox：感叹诈骗手段的创造力不断提升，使得网络欺诈更加猖獗。
• BMaronge：认为文章对链接跳转多次的解释不够清晰，质疑诈骗者为何不直接跳转。
• HocusLocus：分享了帮助家人防范诈骗的经验，强调对老年人的网络安全教育重要性，并提到国家行为者参与的网络诈骗问题。
• username223：质疑为何JavaScript能够发送操作系统级别的通知，认为应限制不可信代码的运行权限，避免将“开放网络”变成攻击面。
• tehwebguy：庆幸某些移动平台不允许浏览器推送通知，认为这是有效的防范措施。
• StuntPope：对文章中提到的“克里姆林宫虚假信息”持怀疑态度，认为Krebs的文章带有偏见，并质疑其专业性。
• wwn_se：推荐使用Adblock作为解决方案，建议为家人和朋友启用广告拦截以防止被骗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是浏览器在处理推送通知和其他权限请求时的用户界面设计是否合理，thyristan对此提出详细批评并建议改进。
• 另一个讨论点是为何诈骗者要通过多个域名跳转来引导用户访问虚假内容，justusthane和BMaronge对此表示不解。
• 对Krebs文章中提到的“克里姆林宫虚假信息”存在不同看法，HocusLocus和StuntPope对此有不同解读和评价。
• 对于如何防范此类诈骗，用户提出了不同建议，包括设置浏览器自动拒绝通知、使用Adblock、以及加强网络安全教育等。

44263780.article_content:
Late last year, security researchers made a startling discovery: Kremlin-backed disinformation campaigns were bypassing moderation on social media platforms by leveraging the same malicious advertising technology that powers a sprawling ecosystem of online hucksters and website hackers. A new report on the fallout from that investigation finds this dark ad tech industry is far more resilient and incestuous than previously known.
Image: Infoblox.
In November 2024, researchers at the security firm
Qurium
published an investigation into “
Doppelganger
,” a disinformation network that promotes pro-Russian narratives and infiltrates Europe’s media landscape by pushing fake news through a network of cloned websites.
Doppelganger campaigns use specialized links that bounce the visitor’s browser through a long series of domains before the fake news content is served. Qurium
found
Doppelganger relies on a sophisticated “domain cloaking” service, a technology that allows websites to present different content to search engines compared to what regular visitors see. The use of cloaking services helps the disinformation sites remain online longer than they otherwise would, while ensuring that only the targeted audience gets to view the intended content.
Qurium discovered that Doppelganger’s cloaking service also promoted online dating sites, and shared much of the same infrastructure with
VexTrio
, which is thought to be the oldest malicious traffic distribution system (TDS) in existence. While TDSs are commonly used by legitimate advertising networks to manage traffic from disparate sources and to track who or what is behind each click, VexTrio’s TDS largely manages web traffic from victims of phishing, malware, and social engineering scams.
BREAKING BAD
Digging deeper, Qurium noticed Doppelganger’s cloaking service used an Internet provider in Switzerland as the first entry point in a chain of domain redirections. They also noticed the same infrastructure hosted a pair of co-branded affiliate marketing services that were driving traffic to sketchy adult dating sites:
LosPollos[.]com
and
TacoLoco[.]co
.
The LosPollos ad network incorporates many elements and references from the hit series “Breaking Bad,” mirroring the fictional “Los Pollos Hermanos” restaurant chain that served as a money laundering operation for a violent methamphetamine cartel.
The LosPollos advertising network invokes characters and themes from the hit show Breaking Bad. The logo for LosPollos (upper left) is the image of Gustavo Fring, the fictional chicken restaurant chain owner in the show.
Affiliates who sign up with LosPollos are given JavaScript-heavy “
smartlinks
” that drive traffic into the VexTrio TDS, which in turn distributes the traffic among a variety of advertising partners, including dating services, sweepstakes offers, bait-and-switch mobile apps, financial scams and malware download sites.
LosPollos affiliates typically stitch these smart links into
WordPress
websites that have been hacked via known vulnerabilities, and those affiliates will earn a small commission each time an Internet user referred by any of their hacked sites falls for one of these lures.
The Los Pollos advertising network promoting itself on LinkedIn.
According to Qurium, TacoLoco is a traffic monetization network that uses deceptive tactics to trick Internet users into enabling “push notifications,” a
cross-platform browser standard
that allows websites to show pop-up messages which appear outside of the browser. For example, on Microsoft Windows systems these notifications typically show up in the bottom right corner of the screen — just above the system clock.
In the case of VexTrio and TacoLoco, the notification approval requests themselves are deceptive — disguised as “CAPTCHA” challenges designed to distinguish automated bot traffic from real visitors. For years, VexTrio and its partners have successfully tricked countless users into enabling these site notifications, which are then used to continuously pepper the victim’s device with a variety of phony virus alerts and misleading pop-up messages.
Examples of VexTrio landing pages that lead users to accept push notifications on their device.
According to
a December 2024 annual report
from
GoDaddy
,
nearly 40 percent of compromised websites in 2024 redirected visitors to VexTrio via LosPollos smartlinks
.
ADSPRO AND TEKNOLOGY
On November 14, 2024, Qurium

data.title: Have a damaged painting? Restore it in just hours with an AI-generated “mask”
data.author: WithinReason
data.article_summary: 麻省理工学院的研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种使用数字构造膜物理修复原始画作的新方法。该方法通过打印极薄的聚合物膜，形成一个可以对齐并粘贴到画作上的“面具”，以覆盖和修复受损区域，且该膜可以轻松移除。这种技术可以在几个小时内完成传统修复方法需要数周甚至更长时间的工作。例如，Kachkine在3.5小时内修复了一幅15世纪的油画，而传统方法可能需要更久。同时，数字记录可以保存修复细节，供未来修复者参考。不过，Kachkine也强调，任何修复都应与了解画作历史和来源的保护专家协商，以确保修复的伦理性和适当性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术品修复中的技术应用（特别是AI）及其伦理问题

不同观点：
• **Daub**：对艺术品修复持批评态度，认为过去的修复项目往往造成了对艺术品的破坏。他举例提到西斯廷教堂天花板的修复项目，认为选择了错误的假设（即米开朗基罗没有对壁画进行任何修正），从而破坏了原作。他还提到维多利亚时代对雕塑的过度清洗以及现代修复者根据客户喜好更改艺术品元素的做法，认为这些都是对艺术品的不当处理。

• **contravariant**：对修复方法的兴趣大于AI本身，但认为声称使用AI可能是为了获得资金支持。这暗示了技术应用中的营销和资金需求问题。

• **bee_rider**：提出艺术家原始意图与修复之间的关系，认为是否应该恢复艺术品是一个值得讨论的问题。同时，也提到艺术品随着时间老化所带来的历史故事，可能不应仅由艺术家决定是否修复。

• **t43562**：建议可以完全不触碰原作，而是通过复制品进行展示和保护，从而避免对原作的任何潜在破坏。

• **matt3210**：质疑是否需要通过AI生成新画作，并提出如果大部分画面被掩盖，那么原作是否还能被称为画作的问题。

• **ecocentrik**：认为即使AI修复技术完美无缺，改变艺术品的展示方式（如包裹艺术品）也会影响观众的体验，从而改变艺术的本质。

• **zelphirkalt**：对AI在修复中的实际作用持怀疑态度，认为大部分工作可能是机械性的，AI可能只涉及颜色推断或遮罩预测。同时质疑谁来负责历史准确性的确认。

• **omoikane**：担心数字记录的长期可读性问题，提出即使有数字记录，也需要定期更新以确保其可用性。

• **zelikane**：引用xkcd漫画，幽默地指出技术修复中可能出现的长期问题。

补充讨论：
• **not_your_mentat**：以幽默的方式提到可以在损坏的部分填充“无象”（no elephants），暗示修复过程中可能会加入不合适的元素。

• **amelius**：幽默地表达了对AI生成不准确部分（如七根手指的手）的担忧，反映了人们对AI技术在艺术领域应用的潜在不信任。

争议焦点：
• 修复技术（尤其是AI）是否应该在艺术品修复中广泛应用，以及如何平衡艺术家的原始意图、历史故事和现代观众的观赏需求。
• 艺术品修复的伦理问题，包括是否应该完全避免对原作的任何改动，以及谁有权决定修复的方式和程度。

Art restoration takes steady hands and a discerning eye. For centuries, conservators have restored paintings by identifying areas needing repair, then mixing an exact shade to fill in one area at a time. Often, a painting can have thousands of tiny regions requiring individual attention. Restoring a single painting can take anywhere from a few weeks to over a decade.
In recent years, digital restoration tools have opened a route to creating virtual representations of original, restored works. These tools apply techniques of computer vision, image recognition, and color matching, to generate a “digitally restored” version of a painting relatively quickly.
Still, there has been no way to translate digital restorations directly onto an original work, until now. In a
paper
appearing today in the journal
Nature
, Alex Kachkine, a mechanical engineering graduate student at MIT, presents a new method he’s developed to physically apply a digital restoration directly onto an original painting.
The restoration is printed on a very thin polymer film, in the form of a mask that can be aligned and adhered to an original painting. It can also be easily removed. Kachkine says that a digital file of the mask can be stored and referred to by future conservators, to see exactly what changes were made to restore the original painting.
“Because there’s a digital record of what mask was used, in 100 years, the next time someone is working with this, they’ll have an extremely clear understanding of what was done to the painting,” Kachkine says. “And that’s never really been possible in conservation before.”
As a demonstration, he applied the method to a highly damaged 15th century oil painting. The method automatically identified 5,612 separate regions in need of repair, and filled in these regions using 57,314 different colors. The entire process, from start to finish, took 3.5 hours, which he estimates is about 66 times faster than traditional restoration methods.
Kachkine acknowledges that, as with any restoration project, there are ethical issues to consider, in terms of whether a restored version is an appropriate representation of an artist’s original style and intent. Any application of his new method, he says, should be done in consultation with conservators with knowledge of a painting’s history and origins.

data.title: Infinite Grid of Resistors
data.author: niklasbuschmann
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个经典的电阻网格谜题，该网格由无限延伸的方形晶格组成，每对相邻节点之间有一个电阻R。文章主要探讨如何计算相邻节点之间的有效电阻。通过考虑电流场的对称性和叠加原理，文章得出相邻节点间的有效电阻为R/2。这种方法类似于电偶极子的电势场分析，利用了拉普拉斯方程的对称性。然而，文章也指出，该推导依赖于一些假设，例如电流在“无限远处”的行为，而这些假设并未完全严谨证明。特别是，将电流注入无限网格的设想存在问题，因为理论上节点到无限远的电阻是无限大的。尽管如此，通过简单对称性得出的结果R/2与其他方法验证结果一致。文章最后提到，要使论证更严谨，可以考虑有限大小的网格。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无限电阻网格问题的相关性和实际应用的讨论，包括电阻网格的理论分析、实际工程中的应用及其教学价值。

不同观点：
• [bgnnn] 认为无限电阻网格问题与实际世界问题相关，特别是在集成电路中的硅基板噪声耦合问题。他强调了网格结构在实际工程中的应用，例如通过分布基板接点来收集噪声电流。
• [neepi] 指出，从实际测量的角度来看，问题在于如何测量，尤其是在考虑分布式电感和电容元件时。数学角度和工程角度存在分歧。
• [kayson] 认为更具教育意义的做法是讨论立方体对角电阻问题，这有助于建立电路对称性和基尔霍夫定律（KCL）等直觉，而不是专注于无限网格问题。
• [bilsbie] 提出一个衍生问题，即为什么不通过减小电线直径来制造电阻，认为这样可能比将电流转化为热量更有效率。
• [TheOtherHobbes] 认为无限网格问题是一个无意义的问题，因为在数学上会导致不确定的无穷大/无穷大结果，建议将时间用于更有意义的问题。

补充讨论：
• [dogman1050] 指出该问题可以视为“薄层电阻”的特例，并提供了一个维基百科链接。
• [praptak] 对对称性和叠加原理的应用提出疑问，质疑为何两个节点的电流可以简单地视为两个单独节点电流的和。
• [bilsbie] 进一步提问，为什么真空不能被视为一个无限电阻网格。
• [quibono] 对对称性和叠加解释中的方向性选择提出疑问，不明白为何一个方向与其他两个方向不同。
• [pyman] 提供了关于无限电阻网格的一个具体结果，指出相邻点之间的电阻大约是三分之一电阻值。
• [at_a_remove] 分享了与渗透理论相关的实际项目经验，描述了通过导电墨水制作不同网格并测量电阻的实验过程。

争议焦点：
• 无限电阻网格问题是否具有实际工程相关性及其在教学中的价值。
• 对称性和叠加原理在分析无限电阻网格中的适用性和解释方式。
• 实际测量中的可行性和理论分析的复杂性。

这些讨论展示了理论问题在实际应用和教学中的不同视角，以及对复杂电路问题分析方法的深入探讨。

Infinite Grid of
Resistors
Remain, remain thou here,
While
sense can keep it on. And, sweetest, fairest,
As
I my poor self did exchange for you,
To
your so infinite loss, so in our trifles
I
still win of you: for my sake wear this...
Shakespeare
There is a well-known puzzle based on the premise of an
infinite grid of resistors connecting adjacent nodes of a square lattice. A
small portion of such a grid is illustrated below.
Between every pair of adjacent nodes is a resistance R,
and were told that this grid of resistors extends to infinity in all
direction, and were asked to determine the effective resistance between two
adjacent nodes, or, more generally, between any two specified nodes of the
lattice.
For adjacent nodes, the usual solution of this puzzle is
to consider the current flow field as the sum of two components, one being
the flow field of a grid with current injected into a single node, and the
other being the flow field of a grid with current extracted from a single
(adjacent) node. The symmetry of the two individual cases then enables us to
infer the flow rates through the immediately adjacent resistors, and hence we
can conclude (as explained in more detail below) that the effective
resistance between two adjacent nodes is R/2. This solution has a certain
intuitive plausibility, since its similar to how the potential field of an
electric dipole can be expressed as the sum of the fields of a positive and a
negative charge, each of which is spherically symmetrical about its
respective charge. Just as the electric potential satisfies the Laplace equation, the voltages of the grid nodes satisfy the discrete from of the Laplace equation, which is to say, the voltage at each node is the average of the voltages
of the four surrounding nodes. Its also easy to see that solutions are
additive, in the sense that the sum of any two solutions for given boundary
conditions is a solution for the sum of the boundary conditions.
If we accept the premise of an infinite grid of resistors,
along with some tacit assumption about the behavior of the voltages and
currents at infinity, and if we accept the idea that we can treat the
current fields for the positive and negative nodes separately, and that
applying a voltage to a single node of the infinite grid will result in some
current flow into the grid, the puzzle is easily solved by simple symmetry
considerations. We assert (somewhat naively) that if we inject (say) four

44279181.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个经典的电阻网格谜题，该网格由无限延伸的方形晶格组成，每对相邻节点之间有一个电阻R。文章主要探讨如何计算相邻节点之间的有效电阻。通过考虑电流场的对称性和叠加原理，文章得出相邻节点间的有效电阻为R/2。这种方法类似于电偶极子的电势场分析，利用了拉普拉斯方程的对称性。然而，文章也指出，该推导依赖于一些假设，例如电流在“无限远处”的行为，而这些假设并未完全严谨证明。特别是，将电流注入无限网格的设想存在问题，因为理论上节点到无限远的电阻是无限大的。尽管如此，通过简单对称性得出的结果R/2与其他方法验证结果一致。文章最后提到，要使论证更严谨，可以考虑有限大小的网格。

data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: 鸡眼镜是一种小型眼镜，设计用于防止鸡之间的啄羽和同类相食行为。与遮眼片不同，鸡眼镜允许鸡向前看，同时遮挡特定视野以减少攻击性行为。早期20世纪在美国大规模生产和销售，通常由赛璐珞或铝制成，通过鼻孔固定。一些款式使用玫瑰色镜片，据信能掩盖血液颜色，从而减少啄伤，但效果存在争议。鸡眼镜曾是断喙术的替代方法，但因涉及组织穿刺，在某些国家被禁止。虽然已不再生产，但仍被作为收藏品，并在流行文化中出现。

44244675.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Small eyeglasses made for chickens
1911 newspaper story on chicken eyeglasses from the
Spirit Lake Beacon
(Iowa)
[
1
]
Chicken eyeglasses
, also known as
chicken specs
,
chicken goggles
, generically as
pick guards
, and under other names,
[
2
]
were small
eyeglasses
made for
chickens
intended to prevent
feather pecking
and
cannibalism
. They differ from
blinders
in that they allow the bird to see forward, whereas blinders do not. One variety used
rose-colored
lenses, as the coloring was thought to prevent a chicken wearing them from recognizing blood on other chickens, which may increase the tendency for
abnormal injurious behavior
. They were
mass-produced
and sold throughout the United States as early as the beginning of the 20th century.
[
3
]
[
4
]
Description and purpose
[
edit
]
Chicken eyeglasses were often made from celluloid or aluminum
[
5
]
and typically consisted of "two oval panels that fit over the upper beak of the chicken. A pin is put through the nostril to hold the oval pieces in place."
[
2
]
Different designs were produced that attached to the chicken's head in different ways. Some were held in place by a strap,
[
3
]
some by small hooks into the
nares
(nostrils) and some by piercing the bone
septum
between the nostrils with a
cotter pin
.
[
6
]
Due to the piercing of tissue, this last type of design is illegal in some countries.
[fn. 1]
Some versions of the devices had semi- or fully transparent lenses, whereas others were tinted, often red- or rose-colored. Other designs were
blinders
, which are opaque and prevent entirely forward vision.
[
2
]
[
7
]
The intended purposes of chicken eyeglasses were to prevent aggressive pecking, cannibalism, and feather pecking.
Chicken eyeglasses are an alternative to
beak trimming
, which removes approximately one-third of the beak by a cold or heated blade or an infrared beam, usually when chicks are one day old. Beak trimming is often effective in reducing pecking injuries but causes pain and significantly affects chicken welfare.
[
7
]
[
8
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
[
11
]
Red-tinted lenses
[
edit
]
Red-tinted lenses were considered effective in reducing internecine pecking because they disguise the color of blood.
[
7
]
As summed up in a 1953 article in Indiana's
National Road Traveler
newspaper, "The deep rose-colored plastic lenses make it impossible for the cannibal [chicken] to see blood on the other chickens, although permitting it to see the grain on the ground."
[
12
]
Elmer Haas of the National Band & Tag Company, a major producer of rose-colored chicken eyeglasses, whose grandfather had devised wireframes for chickens in 1902,
[
13
]
indicated that he believed the purported blood-masking effect of the rose coloring was a myth: "the firm added the rose-colored glasses because it indulged the chicken owners ... [c]hickens are color blind".
[
13
]
(In fact, chickens, like other birds, have good
color vision
.
[
14
]
)  The firm had added the rose-colored feature to its glasses in 1939 under the brand name "Anti-Pix."
[
15
]
This variety of eyeglasses was more complicated than others because the red lenses were fixed to a hinge at the top of the frame. As the hen lowered its head to feed, the lens swung out, giving it an unobstructed view of the ground. When the hen raised her head, as she would during aggression, the lens would swing down giving the hen a red-tinted perception of the environment.
[
16
]
Rose-colored
contact lenses
, rather than eyeglasses, have also been proposed to reduce cannibalism in chickens.
[
17
]
History
[
edit
]
Detail from a 1903 patent filed by Andrew Jackson Jr.
A form of chicken eyeglasses was first patented in 1903 by Andrew Jackson Jr. of
Munich
,
Tennessee
, as an "Eye-protector for chickens."
[
18
]
In the U.S., they were available through the mail order company
Sears-Roebuck
or chicken feed stores for a few cents.
[
19
]
The eyeglasses are no longer produced by the National Band & Tag Company, but are sought as
collector's items
.
[
6
]
Using chicken eyeglasses was still practiced in 1973, evidenced by Illinois'
The Hawk-Eye
newspaper that a farmer had 8,000 chickens fitted with the rose-colored variety.
[
20
]
One inventor of a form of the glasses proposed legislation in
Kansas
to require
all
chickens in the state to be fitted with glasses, but his campaign was unsuccessful.
[
21
]
In popular culture
[
edit
]
On January 16, 1955, Sam Nadler of the National Farm Equipment Company of Brooklyn appeared on
CBS
' popular primetime television show,
What's My Line?
[
22
]
The show was in the format of a
guessing game
, in which a panel attempted to determine the line (occupation) of contestants.
[
23
]
Show officials listed Mr. Nadler's occupation for the audience as "sells 'eyeglasses' for chickens". After the panel was unsuccessful in guessing his occupation,  Mr. Nadler's identity was revealed, and he stated that his company sold 2–3 million pairs of chicken eyeglasses annually.

data.title: Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
data.author: luuio
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者作为初级开发人员时在一家公司经历的数据库使用不当的问题。最初，公司的关键系统依赖于包含大量存储过程的SQL Server数据库，这些存储过程包含复杂的业务逻辑，导致API调用占用大量数据库服务器CPU资源，并且由于查询计划的变化经常引发超时和死锁，最终导致系统可靠性下降。为了解决这些问题，公司决定进行系统重写，但新的设计完全摒弃了关系型数据库，转而采用简单的键值存储（Key-Value stores）。然而，这种设计并不适合高度关系型的数据模型，导致了一系列新的问题。文章强调了从错误中学习的重要性，并反思了设计选择对系统的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：存储过程（stored procedures）在现代开发中的使用及其优劣

不同观点：
• freetime2：认为存储过程在过去的项目中导致了技术债务，因为开发人员不敢或不愿意更新它们，最终导致了代码库的混乱。这种经历促使团队决定重写整个应用程序并转向NoSQL数据库。
• Quarrelsome：指出关于技术选择的争论往往带有宗教色彩。批评了对ORMs和存储过程的极端看法，认为两者都有其适用的场景。存储过程使用不当可能导致问题，但完全否定RDBMS的作用也是一种误解。
• tanelpoder：认为开发人员不愿意使用存储过程既是技能问题也是意愿问题。在处理数据负载和验证数据流时，存储过程可以提高性能和效率，减少复杂性。
• branko_d：反驳了对存储过程效率的常见批评，指出存储过程在CPU使用和查询计划缓存方面可能更有效率。强调无论是存储过程还是客户端提交的查询，都需要良好的索引和查询优化。
• bazoom42：存储过程在批量数据操作中表现出色，但在逐行处理数据或包含过多业务逻辑时可能导致问题。主张根据具体任务选择合适的工具。
• marc_abonce：认为技术决策和公司财务表现之间没有必然联系。虽然好的代码有其内在价值，但不一定直接带来经济利益。
• t43562：基于多次重写项目的经验，认为大多数重写项目都不是好主意。渐进式改进现有系统通常比彻底重写更有效。
• m_ransing：提到现代关系数据库支持JSON API，可以通过这些API减少一些不必要的检查点。
• jrochkind1：讨论了一种优化写操作的方案，使用乐观锁机制，指出如果数据库支持条件写操作，可以避免额外的读写操作。

• cl0ckt0wer和kragen：对原文中一些用词和作者身份的轻松评论，不涉及技术讨论。
• zupa-hu和gxs：对文章的阅读体验发表看法，一个表示没有结论，另一个表示欣赏文章的多角度分析。

• 存储过程的使用场景及其优劣：一方认为存储过程导致技术债务和维护困难，另一方认为在特定场景下存储过程能提高性能和效率。

总结：讨论主要围绕存储过程在现代开发中的适用性及其优缺点展开，参与者提供了不同的实际经验和理论分析。

Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
Date: June 11, 2025
Tags:
software development
Disclaimer: This story took place when I was a junior developer for a previous employer ages ago. Some details might be fuzzy, and goes without saying this is entirely from my own POV so take everything here with humor and a grain of salt.
I like to share these stories, because I believe learning what
not
to do is just as valuable as learning what to do.
The setup
The team I joined was part of a larger org. This org inherited a highly critical pipeline from an offshore team. When I say critical, I mean the-entire-company-bottom-line-and-financials-depended-on-them critical. I guess the company just wanted to move that particularly branch of development back to the US. These systems were complex with a lot of business rules and many moving parts, multiple large code bases, and definitely ancient.
The development experience wasn’t great either. Even though there were separate codebases, the projects were somehow setup in a way that changing one small file required building almost the entire thing (which took about 15-30 minutes). The build process also depended on the underlying operating system components, thus development had to happen inside a VM. Each VM had a “dev” version of the entire pipeline deployed, that’s the only way one could exercise the code while under development. Then one would have to know which DDL files they needed to copy from the build output to the local “dev” deployment and restart all the right Windows services in order to test their changes.
Tests were flaky, outages all the time, random hidden undocumented features everywhere. Things were… quirkly, to say the least. One particular quirk that’s the main character of this story is the databases–the main source of the outages, as I could remember.
The pendulum swung left: the old database
All the data for this pipeline was spread across multiple SQL Server databases, across different servers. That wasn’t the problem. The problem was that a lot of business logic was baked into pages and pages of stored procedures, with joint after joint after joint that would put Snoop to shame. Why was it written that way? Nobody knew. Perhaps some small part of the original team got tired of the bad development process, and it was quicker to just update stored procedures than having to wait for half an hour for compilation.
Thinking back, the data wasn’t modeled badly either. Even more than a decade later, I still think that the domain is pretty complex, and the data was modeled as well as anyone could have.
This little quirk meant a few things:
Many critical APIs call would spend most of its CPU time inside the finite database servers. New APIs, or updating existing APIs meant you were hogging the DB/CPU time from every one else.
API latency was at the mercy of the Query Planner. Any slight change in data statistics or business logic would cause the a different Query Plan to be picked, which drastically changed the execution time, and usually caused timeouts. A hash join suddenly became a full table scan across billions of rows without any warning.
The cherry on top of all that was the entire pipeline, from stored procedure to managed and native code, heavily used
MSDTC
–which was brital and proned to deadlocks.
All of this tanked the pipeline reliability. Downtime was largely due to deadlocks, or some query timing out, which had been running just fine minutes earlier.
To this org’s credit, they put a lot of time and effort into improving things, and made a lot of progress, but a rewrite was inevitable.
Interlude:
I will refrain from discussing whether a rewrite was truly necessary. I didn’t know all the details then, and I don’t know all the details now. But we can discuss the design choices of the rewrite.
The pendulum swung right: the new design
Perhaps due to the scars from the existing database issues, “the architects” decided they wanted nothing to do with relational databases, nor stored procedure, nor query plans. They wanted everything to be written into simple primitive Key-Value stores for their new design.
Each instance of these key value stores provided exactly 4 and only 4 operations: Read one key, Insert one key/value pair, Update key/value pair, Delete one key. No transactions, no batching, nothing else.
For some products, that’s perfectly fine, but not for this pipeline. And here comes a chain of “fun” events, one influenced by a previous decision:
The data schema
The data for this domain is highly relational, but perhaps modeling things the right way, it could still work with a KV store. Instead of modeling things in a relational manner, one could write nested documents, and embed the child elements inside the parent document. So to get the items related to a parent object, one just loads the entire document for the parent object, no need for fancy joints.

44260964.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者作为初级开发人员时在一家公司经历的数据库使用不当的问题。最初，公司的关键系统依赖于包含大量存储过程的SQL Server数据库，这些存储过程包含复杂的业务逻辑，导致API调用占用大量数据库服务器CPU资源，并且由于查询计划的变化经常引发超时和死锁，最终导致系统可靠性下降。为了解决这些问题，公司决定进行系统重写，但新的设计完全摒弃了关系型数据库，转而采用简单的键值存储（Key-Value stores）。然而，这种设计并不适合高度关系型的数据模型，导致了一系列新的问题。文章强调了从错误中学习的重要性，并反思了设计选择对系统的影响。

• 技术决策与经济效益之间的关系：marc_abonce认为技术决策对公司财务影响不大，而其他人可能认为技术债务和不良决策会导致实际问题。

总结：讨论主要围绕存储过程在现代开发中的适用性及其优缺点展开，参与者提供了不同的实际经验和理论分析。

data.title: Clinical knowledge in LLMs does not translate to human interactions
data.author: insistent
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在医疗诊断中的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby认为，LLM在诊断中难以有效提取必要信息，因为患者可能遗漏或隐瞒信息，即使在模拟场景中也会发生这种情况。这与临床医生的能力有差距。
• hackitup7分享了个人经验，指出ChatGPT在多次测试中表现良好，尤其在提供详细和诚实信息的情况下，能够匹配医生的诊断，但也有少数错误，特别是在症状变化的情况下。
• dosinga指出，LLM在诊断和建议治疗方面表现良好，但在自诊情况下，由于人类用户的问题，效果不佳。
• twotwotwo讨论了在工作环境中使用LLM时的提示问题，强调需要明确的指示和信息检索能力，并建议通过训练和工具改进解决这些问题。
• keeptrying提到LLM在指导治疗时会出现细微错误，并认为医学教育和医生行为与普通用户有巨大差距，这影响了LLM的有效使用。
• cckolon引用其医生妻子的话，认为人类医生也面临类似的问题，暗示这不是LLM独有的问题。
• callc关注LLM在医疗应用中的责任和经济动机，质疑医疗提供者是否愿意为LLM的输出承担责任，并考虑成本和可及性问题。
• wongarsu建议设置更多对照组（如有无人类或LLM辅助）以更好地评估LLM的实际效果，并指出需要基准来衡量“良好”表现。
• pyman认为LLM缺乏与真实患者互动的社交技能，可能是知识以外的瓶颈。
• dhash对研究表示赞赏，并提出未来研究方向，包括与专家用户比较、LLM对医疗结果的影响和后续行为。

补充讨论：
• ekianjo提出一个有争议的观点，认为如果LLM的表现与对照组无异，是否意味着可以无损失地取代人类。这引发了关于LLM在医疗中角色的更深层次讨论。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在医疗诊断中的有效性和可靠性，特别是在自诊和责任承担方面。
• 重要的论据包括临床医生的信息提取能力、用户对LLM的信任度、模型在真实场景中的局限性以及医疗责任和经济因素。

data.title: AMD's AI Future Is Rack Scale 'Helios'
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD的ROCm平台及其在GPGPU市场中的竞争力，特别是与NVIDIA CUDA的对比，以及用户对AMD软件支持和硬件性能的评价。

不同观点：
• **ROCm的实用性问题**：Minks指出，ROCm在不同使用场景下表现不稳定，尤其是在消费级显卡上的支持不足，导致其不得不转向CUDA以节省时间和减少麻烦。相比之下，CUDA的工作流更加顺畅，而运行MiOpen基准测试耗时过长。

• **AMD与NVIDIA的竞争**：alecco认为，NVIDIA的CUDA生态系统已经非常成熟，大多数人不会冒险学习一个市场份额不到10%的架构（指ROCm）。AMD需要在软件栈的优化上多下功夫，而不仅仅是推出更强的硬件。

• **AMD软件栈的复杂性**：AlexanderDhoore表示，AMD提供的软件选项繁多且复杂，导致用户在选择时感到困惑，尤其是对于神经网络推理和训练的SDK。相比NVIDIA的CUDA，AMD的软件策略显得不够清晰。

• **对ROCm的未来展望**：Paradigma11和kombine对AMD的未来抱有期待，认为AMD需要在硬件性能上追赶NVIDIA的H100等高端芯片。然而，这种未来尚未实现，用户需要等待。

• **ROCm对普通用户的影响**：numpad0指出，对于普通AI用户而言，ROCm的支持并不关键，因为AMD的消费级显卡已经通过Vulkan API提供了足够的支持，尽管速度较慢。许多轻量级的AI应用也支持Vulkan。

• **对AMD的批评**：halJordan对AMD的ROCm支持表示强烈不满，指出AMD在RDNA4系列发布后四个月内都没有提供支持，认为AMD在性能数据上存在误导性宣传。

• **对AMD未来性能的质疑**：zombiwoof认为，AMD的未来应该聚焦于如何实现其声称的性能数据，而不是仅仅宣称高性能。

补充讨论：
• **对AMD管理层的质疑**：user____name提到了对AMD管理层的质疑，问及Bob Page是否负责相关工作，暗示对领导层的信心不足。

• **情感反应**：aetherspawn对每次有关AMD的新闻都产生情感反应，引用“Atropos log, abandoning Helios”来表达对AMD在ROCm上的失望。

争议焦点：
• **ROCm与CUDA的实用性对比**：部分用户认为CUDA在实际应用中更为成熟和便捷，而ROCm的支持和性能存在不足。
• **AMD软件支持的混乱**：用户对AMD提供的软件选项感到困惑，认为其缺乏清晰的战略方向。
• **AMD硬件性能的期望与现实**：用户对AMD未来硬件性能的期望很高，但现实中对其表现存在质疑和批评。

总结：用户对AMD的ROCm平台存在不同的看法，主要集中在ROCm与CUDA的对比、AMD软件支持的复杂性以及硬件性能的期望与现实之间的差距。批评主要集中在ROCm的实用性和AMD在软件支持上的不足。

data.title: Fixing the mechanics of my bullet chess
data.author: tibbar
data.article_summary: 作者Jacob Brazeal分享了他下国际象棋时的一个发现。他一直擅长快棋（blitz），但在超快棋（bullet）中表现较差。最近，他改变了移动棋子的方式，从拖放（drag-and-drop）改为点击（click-and-click），结果每步平均节省0.25秒，使他的超快棋等级分（ELO）提高了约100分。点击移动不仅更快，尤其是在长距离移动棋子时，还能更好地预判走子，避免失误。这一改变让作者在超快棋中思考时间更充裕，减少了仓促走子导致的错误，缩小了与快棋的等级分差距。他感叹这一简单的技术调整竟然带来显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：国际象棋中不同操作方式（点击 vs 拖动）的效率以及它们对玩家评分（ELO）和游戏形式（线上 vs 线下）的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持点击操作**：helloplanets认为触摸屏（尤其是平板电脑）非常适合快棋，可以通过点击快速移动棋子。tyzoid也表示点击方式减少了误操作的可能性。
• **支持拖动操作**：jpablo和fasterik认为拖动操作比点击更快，因为减少了多余的点击动作，并且可以在等待对手走棋时预览走子，从而避免错误。fasterik还指出，许多顶级快棋玩家（如Andrew Tang、Hikaru Nakamura）使用拖动操作。
• **个人习惯影响**：quasigloam提到自己习惯使用拖动操作，但觉得点击操作也差不多速度，只是不常用。Andrew Tang使用拖动操作，而Magnus Carlsen使用点击操作但依然在快棋中表现出色。

补充讨论：
• **ELO评分的跨平台差异**：ukprogrammer提出在线上的ELO评分似乎并不能完全反映到线下棋局中，认为身体操作对游戏的影响出乎意料地大。
• **不同棋类形式的ELO差异**：b2fel认为快棋和超快棋（bullet）之间的ELO差异是系统本身的特性，每个玩家都会出现这种情况。
• **速度对评分的意义**：not-so-darkstar认为速度在低端局中更为重要，可能影响评分。
• **平板设备操作的讨论**：helpfulContrib好奇在平板设备上用手指拖动操作的效果如何。

争议焦点：

44279579.article_content:
Jacob Brazeal
Uncategorized
June 14, 2025
1 Minute
I’ve been playing chess a
long time
now, and I’ve always been a good deal better (maybe a couple hundred ELO points) at blitz (3+0 or 5+0) than bullet (1+0). Well, I may have just fixed that. I changed how I move pieces this afternoon and have gained about 100 ELO already. When I play on a computer, I usually drag-and-drop pieces. But it turns out you can also move pieces by clicking first on your piece and then the target square. An analysis of my recent games indicates this shift saved me about 0.25 seconds per move, shifting from an average of around 1.8 seconds/move to 1.6 seconds/move. I can’t believe I never figured this out before.
The graph above compares a 25-game rolling average of my ELO vs. average seconds per move over the last 100 games. Ithink there are a couple things going on:
click-and-click ™ is physically faster than drag-and-drop, especially when the piece is moving a long way.
click-and-click allows a better alternative to pre-moving, which matters a lot in bullet chess. You can click the piece you think you’ll move before your opponent moves, and then if the move still works, you can instantly click the target square. But if the move actually doesn’t work, then you can avoid the blunder.
It
feels
like I have just enough time to actually think through my moves now.  Historically I’m usually so short on time in bullet chess that I end up pre-moving a lot of the game, or otherwise rushing, with all the associated blunders. This change in mechanics has cut the difference between my blitz and bullet ELOs in half, and I think if I keep playing, the difference will continue to drop.
Has everyone else been doing click-and-click this whole time instead of drag-and-drop? Sheesh!

data.title: Using `make` to compile C programs
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了在不同系统上编译C/C++程序的基本步骤和常见问题，主要以Mac系统为例。具体步骤包括：

1. **安装C编译器**：在Ubuntu上可以通过`sudo apt-get install build-essential`安装，而在Mac上需要安装Xcode命令行工具。
2. **安装程序依赖**：C语言没有依赖管理器，需要手动安装。可以通过系统的包管理器安装，例如在Debian系统上使用`apt`。在Mac上使用Homebrew，但要注意包名的不同。
3. **运行`./configure`（如果需要）**：有些程序需要运行此脚本来生成`Makefile`。
4. **运行`make`编译**：使用`make`命令编译程序，如果出错，通常是依赖问题。需要根据错误信息调整编译器和链接器的参数。

文中还提到编译分为编译和链接两个步骤，需要正确设置编译器和链接器的环境变量以找到依赖库。例如，遇到`library not found`错误时，需要指定库的路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Makefile及相关构建工具、变量和构建系统的工作原理及其优缺点。

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 详细解释了CPPFLAGS、CXXFLAGS、LDFLAGS和LDLIBS的区别和用途。强调了CPPFLAGS与C预处理器（cpp程序）有关，而CXXFLAGS专用于C++。同时，LDFLAGS和LDLIBS在链接过程中有不同的作用，前者用于早期选项，后者用于库选项。

• [ashishb] 赞赏Makefile的简洁和通用性，尤其是在不同编程语言项目中的应用，如Go、Rust、Python等。他认为即使底层构建工具变化，高层次的`make`命令（如`make format`、`make build`）仍然保持不变，提供了跨项目的稳定性。

• [jwrallie] 提出可以不用Makefile直接使用Make构建单文件C程序，这种直接调用`make file`的方式让他感到惊讶，表明Make的灵活性。

• [brunokim] 对Autotools持保留态度，认为虽然Autotools通过编译测试环境具有一定优势，但希望不必深入学习其工作原理。

• [diimdeep] 质疑当前不同编程语言需要不同构建工具的现状，并分享了一些已经尝试简化这一问题的项目链接，如nob.h项目。

• [jiehong] 希望更多项目包含Dockerfile，通过Docker提供一个包含编译器和所有依赖的镜像，从而简化构建过程，特别是在跨架构的情况下。

• [singpolyma3] 反驳“C语言没有依赖管理器”的观点，认为有很多工具可以用于C的依赖管理，如apt、cargo、homebrew和rubygems。

• [zabzonk] 提到“C/C++”这一表述，暗示使用时需要谨慎区分C和C++。

• [o11c] 补充了许多构建过程中的细节，如`build-essential`安装包的组成、`pkg-config`用于列出已安装的依赖、`autoreconf -i`用于生成`configure`脚本等。他还指出了`./configure`和`make`在处理库变量时的不一致性，并提供了相关文档参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是构建工具的选择和复杂性。例如，[brunokim]和[o11c]对Autotools的态度不同，前者希望避免学习，而后者认为在特定情况下Autotools非常有用。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是Makefile的灵活性和跨项目一致性，[ashishb]和[jwrallie]都强调了Makefile在这些方面的优势。
• 最后，关于依赖管理和构建环境配置的讨论，如[singpolyma3]和[o11c]提到的各种工具和方法，也显示出社区对简化C/C++项目构建的持续努力。
